destinations.name: Rishikesh
destinations.tagline: Yoga Capital of the World & Himalayan Adventure Hub
destinations.description: Nestled in the foothills of the Garhwal Himalayas along the sacred Ganges River, Rishikesh blends world-class white water rafting, bungee jumping, and serene yoga ashrams.
destinations.overview: Rishikesh is revered as the Yoga Capital of the World. From the vibrant evening Ganga Aarti at Triveni Ghat to adrenaline-pumping Class IV rafting on the emerald Ganges, it offers the ultimate balance of spirituality and thrill.

faqs.q: Is Rishikesh safe for solo female travellers?
faqs.a: Yes, Rishikesh is one of the safest travel destinations in India with a hospitable spiritual community.
Rafting is typically closed during the monsoon season (July to mid-September) for safety.

destinations.name: Haridwar
destinations.tagline: Gateway to the Gods & Epicentre of Ganga Devotion
destinations.description: One of India’s seven holiest cities where the River Ganges enters the Indo-Gangetic plains. Witness thousands of floating oil lamps during the legendary evening Aarti.
destinations.overview: Haridwar is the sacred entry point for the Char Dham Yatra. Pilgrims flock to Har Ki Pauri to bathe in the holy river, visit Mansa Devi hilltop temple via cable car, and taste iconic street delicacies.

faqs.q: What is the best time to see the Ganga Aarti?
faqs.a: Arrive at Har Ki Pauri around 5:30 PM in winter or 6:30 PM in summer to secure a good viewing spot.

destinations.name: Mussoorie
destinations.tagline: The Queen of the Hills with British Colonial Charm
destinations.description: Perched on a 2,000m ridge facing the snow-clad Garhwal Himalayan peaks, Mussoorie offers misty walking trails, colonial bakeries, and waterfall cascades.
destinations.overview: Mussoorie is famed for its romantic mountain promenade (The Mall Road), vintage English architecture, Kempty Falls, and the majestic Gun Hill sunset viewpoint.
destinations.bestTime: March to June & September to November
thingsToDo: Stroll along Camel’s Back Road at sunset
Cable car ride to Gun Hill

faqs.a: Snowfall typically occurs between late December and early February.

destinations.name: Dehradun
destinations.tagline: Scenic Doon Valley Capital, Forest Academies & Cafes
destinations.description: The green capital city nestled between the Ganga and Yamuna rivers. Renowned for colonial educational institutions, Robber’s Cave, and vibrant cafes on Rajpur Road.
destinations.overview: Dehradun blends cosmopolitan Himalayan lifestyle with deep history. It serves as the primary transport gateway to Mussoorie, Chakrata, and Rishikesh.
destinations.bestTime: All year round (March to June & October to February best)
thingsToDo: Walk inside the river caves of Guchhupani
Explore grand Greco-Roman architecture at FRI
Cafe hopping along Old Rajpur Road

faqs.q: Which is the nearest airport to Rishikesh and Mussoorie?
faqs.a: Jolly Grant Airport (DED) in Dehradun is the closest airport.

destinations.name: Nainital
destinations.tagline: The Shimmering Lake District of Kumaon
destinations.description: Set around an emerald eye-shaped lake, Nainital charms visitors with wooden sailboats, British heritage cottages, and breathtaking viewpoints of Nanda Devi.
destinations.overview: Located at 1,938 meters, Nainital is the crown jewel of Kumaon. Take a wooden yacht ride on Naini Lake, browse Tibetan market stalls, and ride the ropeway to Snow View Point.
destinations.bestTime: March to June & September to November
thingsToDo: Yacht and paddle boating on the lake
Explore candle factories and Tibetan markets

faqs.q: How far is Nainital from Delhi?
faqs.a: Approximately 300 km, taking 6–7 hours by road or express train to Kathgodam.

destinations.name: Kedarnath
destinations.tagline: Lord Shiva’s Highest Jyotirlinga Amidst Glacial Peaks
destinations.description: Perched at 3,584m above sea level near the Mandakini River, the 8th-century stone shrine of Kedarnath is one of Hinduism’s most revered pilgrimage destinations.
destinations.overview: Kedarnath stands against the dramatic backdrop of the 6,940m Kedarnath Peak. Pilgrims undertake a 16 km trek from Gaurikund or book VIP helicopter shuttles from Phata and Guptkashi.
destinations.bestTime: May to June & September to October (temple open 6 months)
thingsToDo: Trek from Gaurikund with alpine valley views

faqs.q: Is biometric registration mandatory for Kedarnath?
faqs.a: Yes, all pilgrims must register on the official Uttarakhand Char Dham portal.

destinations.name: Badrinath
destinations.tagline: The Abode of Lord Badri Narayan & India’s Last Village Mana
destinations.description: Cradled between the Nar and Narayana mountain ranges, Badrinath is the principal Dham dedicated to Lord Vishnu along the holy banks of the Alaknanda River.
destinations.overview: Badrinath features the brightly colored facade of the ancient temple, the natural thermal waters of Tapt Kund, and Mana—the last Indian village bordering Tibet.
destinations.bestTime: May to June & September to October
thingsToDo: Visit Vyas Gufa where Mahabharata was written
Experience tea at India’s First Tea Shop in Mana

faqs.q: Can Badrinath be reached directly by vehicle?
faqs.a: Yes, motorable roads go all the way to Badrinath town.

destinations.name: Auli
destinations.tagline: India’s Skiing Capital & Himalayan Meadow Paradise
destinations.description: Surrounded by coniferous oak forests and panoramic 360-degree views of Nanda Devi and Kamet, Auli is Asia’s highest ski resort with groomed slopes.
destinations.overview: Auli Bugyal lies at 2,800m. In winter it is draped in powder snow ideal for skiing and snowboarding, while in summer it transforms into lush green alpine meadows.
destinations.bestTime: December to March (for skiing) & April to June (for meadows)
thingsToDo: Ride the scenic 4km cable car from Joshimath
Trek through pine woods to Gorson Bugyal

faqs.q: Do beginners get ski equipment in Auli?
faqs.a: Yes, certified rental shops and instructors provide full gear and lessons.

destinations.name: Jim Corbett National Park
destinations.tagline: India’s Legendary Tiger Territory & Dense Sal Wilderness
destinations.description: India’s oldest national park, established in 1936, protecting the majestic Royal Bengal Tiger, wild Asian elephants, leopards, and over 600 bird species.
destinations.overview: Corbett spans 520 sq km across the Shivalik foothills. Explore the Dhikala, Bijrani, and Jhirna safari zones in open 4x4 gypsies.
destinations.bestTime: November to June (Dhikala zone opens November 15)
thingsToDo: Elephant spotting by the Ramganga river
Luxury riverside resort stay with live Kumaoni folk music

faqs.q: How early should Corbett safari permits be booked?
faqs.a: At least 30 to 45 days in advance as forest department permits are strictly limited.

destinations.name: Dhanaulti
destinations.tagline: Quiet Pine Glades, Eco Parks & Himalayan Solitude
destinations.description: Located at 2,286m just 25km beyond Mussoorie, Dhanaulti offers tranquil deodar woods, crisp mountain air, and quiet cottages far from city crowds.
destinations.overview: A peaceful haven known for Eco Parks Amber and Dhara, Surkanda Devi hilltop temple with 360-degree Himalayan views, and apple orchards.

faqs.q: Is Dhanaulti less crowded than Mussoorie?
faqs.a: Yes, Dhanaulti offers a much calmer, nature-first sanctuary.

reviews.author: Sameer Sharma
reviews.title: Serene Ganga views and remarkable hospitality
reviews.comment: Waking up to the morning Ganga Aarti right from the balcony was an unforgettable experience. The breakfast spread was healthy and the staff took care of every request.

reviews.author: Neha Gupta
reviews.title: Life-changing Char Dham experience
reviews.comment: Yatrimap made this arduous Himalayan pilgrimage completely stress-free. Our driver Bhupendra was a mountain master, and the VIP darshan pass saved us 6 hours in line.

reviews.author: Rohan Iyer
reviews.title: Top notch rafting guides and safety
reviews.comment: Done rafting in Colorado and Bali, but the Class IV rapids on the Ganga with Yatrimap were world-class! The cliff jump into the river was thrilling.

blogs.title: The Ultimate Guide to Char Dham Yatra 2026: Route, Helicopter Bookings & Tips
blogs.author: Ananya Sen (Content Specialist)
blogs.excerpt: Everything you need to know before undertaking the sacred journey to Yamunotri, Gangotri, Kedarnath, and Badrinath.
blogs.content: Undertaking the Char Dham Yatra is one of the most spiritually transformative journeys in India. In this guide, we outline the exact chronological circuit starting from Yamunotri and culminating at Badrinath, biometric registration procedures, high altitude acclimatization essentials, and how to secure reliable helicopter shuttles.

blogs.title: Top 10 Hidden Waterfalls & Bohemian Cafes in Rishikesh You Never Knew Existed
blogs.author: Priya Patel (Senior Travel Agent)
blogs.excerpt: Escape the tourist crowds and discover secret plunge pools, vegan sourdough bakeries, and cliffside sunset views.
blogs.content: While Laxman Jhula and Ram Jhula capture most travellers’ attention, Rishikesh holds secluded treasures just a short scooty ride away. From the hidden cascading pools of Patna Waterfall to authentic wood-fired bakeries tucked in Tapovan.

blogs.title: Top 7 High-Altitude Treks in Uttarakhand for Beginners & Pro Trekkers
blogs.author: Vikram Singh Rawat (Expedition Leader)
blogs.excerpt: From the golden sunset slopes of Kedarkantha to the pristine glacial mirrors of Roopkund and Dayara Bugyal.
blogs.content: Uttarakhand offers some of the most dramatic mountain trekking routes anywhere in the world. Whether you are seeking your very first winter summit or aiming for a multi-pass crossing, here is the complete breakdown of trail difficulties, gear lists, best seasons, and safety protocols for high-altitude trekking in the Garhwal and Kumaon Himalayas.

blogs.title: Self-Drive vs Chauffeur Taxis in the Hills: A Complete Traveler Guide
blogs.author: Yatrimap Editorial Team
blogs.excerpt: Weighing safety, road conditions, hairpin bends, driver fatigue, and cost when touring Uttarakhand and Himachal.
blogs.content: Navigating hill roads requires patience, mountain gear management, and experience with hairpin turns. In this comparative guide, we explore when hiring a certified hill chauffeur makes the most sense (Char Dham, high rain seasons, night journeys) versus when a self-drive Thar 4x4 or compact SUV gives you the freedom to explore offbeat camping spots at your own pace.
